subject: sociology
title: Sociological Perspectives: Feminism & Interactionism
welcome_lead: Three feminisms and the micro world of symbolic interaction.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology perspectives feminism Mead Goffman interactionism.
final_note: Macro power and micro meaning — both shape society.

concepts.def: Equality through legal and educational reform.
Mead — meaning emerges in social interaction.
Cooley — self formed by imagined view of others.
Goffman — life is performance with front and back stage.

walkthroughs.body_html: Liberal (Friedan 1963 'The Feminine Mystique'): reform via law. Radical (Firestone 1970): patriarchy is the root of all oppression. Marxist (Benston 1969): women's unpaid domestic labour subsidises capitalism. Black feminism (hooks 1981): white feminism ignores race.

Mead (1934): humans use symbols (language) to construct meaning. Blumer (1969) coined 'symbolic interactionism' — three premises: humans act based on meanings; meanings come from interaction; meanings are revised. Method: ethnography.

Goffman (1959) 'Presentation of Self': life is theatre. Front stage: performance for audience. Back stage: relaxed and authentic. Impression management: tactics to control how others see us. Stigma (1963): spoiled identity managed through concealment.
